description: ASCII merger tree format produced by AHF (Amiga Halo Finder) and its companion MergerTree tool. Per-snapshot halo catalogues are stored in .AHF_halos files; progenitor links (all progenitors with merit scores) are stored in .AHF_croco files; the best-progenitor index is stored in .AHF_mtree_idx files. Halo IDs encode the snapshot number and MPI rank via the SUSSING2013 scheme: ID = snap_id * 1e16 + mpi_rank * 1e10 + halo_1based_index. Trees are reconstructed from the full progenitor graph; pointers are expressed as tree-local flat indices.
references: Knollmann & Knebe (2009), ApJS 182, 608 - AHF: AMIGA's Halo Finder https://doi.org/10.1088/0067-0049/182/2/608
AHF source v1.0-123, analysis/MergerTree/src/libio.c - write_mtree(), libio_halos.c - getHaloID / getSussing2013ID
AHF source v1.0-123, src/libahf/ahf_halos.c - AngMom normalization (lines 4946-4960), sigV definition (line 4687), halo ID encoding (line 2150)

Descendant.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
Descendant.notes: Inverted from AHF_croco progenitor links. Each AHF_croco file for snap N lists progenitors of snap-N halos in snap N-1; the driver inverts these to build a snap-N-1 -> snap-N descendant map. If a progenitor appears in multiple descendant lists (only possible when MTREE_BOTH_WAYS is not set), the descendant with the highest shared-particle merit is kept.

FirstProgenitor.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
FirstProgenitor.notes: The progenitor listed first (highest merit = SharedPart/max(HaloPart_desc, HaloPart_prog)) in the AHF_croco block for each descendant halo. Mapped to tree-local flat index.

NextProgenitor.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
NextProgenitor.notes: The second (and subsequent) progenitors in the AHF_croco list for a given descendant, forming a singly-linked chain. NextProgenitor[FirstProgenitor] = second progenitor, etc. Mapped to tree-local flat indices.

FirstHaloInFOFGroup.source_units: AHF SUSSING2013 halo ID (uint64); 0 = no host (field halo)
FirstHaloInFOFGroup.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
FirstHaloInFOFGroup.notes: AHF hostHaloID encodes the SUSSING2013 ID of the direct parent halo; a value of 0 means the halo is a field/central halo. For SAGE, FirstHaloInFOFGroup must point to the TOP-LEVEL central (the ancestor of the full subhalo hierarchy with hostHaloID=0). The driver traces each halo's hostHaloID chain to find this top-level central.

NextHaloInFOFGroup.source_units: grouping by top-level central at same snapshot
NextHaloInFOFGroup.target_units: integer index within Tree<X> halo array
NextHaloInFOFGroup.notes: Built by grouping all halos at each snapshot that share the same top-level central (the hostHaloID=0 ancestor from get_top_central). Within each group, halos are sorted by Mhalo descending, then the true central (the union-find host, NOT merely the most massive member) is forced to the head of the chain: central -> sat1 -> sat2 -> ... -> -1. This corrects both FirstHaloInFOFGroup and the chain order for stripped centrals, since SAGE's satellite iterator starts at Halo[central].NextHaloInFOFGroup. Implemented via utils.fof_topology.build_fof_chains.

SubhaloLen.notes: Column 5 in AHF_halos. Direct copy of bound particle count.

Group_M_Crit200.notes: Column 4 in AHF_halos. AHF defines the virial mass using the overdensity threshold stored in column 36 (ovdens). For this dataset ovdens=200.00 (critical), so Mhalo is M_200c - a direct match for Group_M_Crit200.

Group_M_Mean200.notes: Not available in AHF output. AHF computes a single virial mass using one overdensity criterion (critical or mean, set at compile/run time). This dataset uses critical (ovdens=200). Using sentinel 0.0.

Group_M_TopHat200.notes: Not available in AHF output. AHF does not separately compute the Bryan & Norman (1998) tophat virial mass. Using sentinel 0.0.

SubhaloPos.notes: Columns 6-8 in AHF_halos. AHF writes positions as pos_code * x_fac * 1000, where x_fac = 1/boxsize converts code units to Mpc/h, so the output is in kpc/h. No scaling required. Output shape (N, 3). On-disk values stored in kpc/h for both output formats: lhalo_hdf5 reader multiplies by 0.001 post-read; binary_writer divides by 1000 before packing.

SubhaloVel.notes: Columns 9-11 in AHF_halos. AHF writes velocities as vel_code * v_fac where v_fac = a * t_unit / boxsize converts to physical peculiar km/s. No scaling required. Output shape (N, 3).

SubhaloVelDisp.notes: Column 19 in AHF_halos. AHF computes sigV = sqrt(sum(|dV|^2 * weight) / M_total) which is the 3D RMS velocity dispersion (sigma_3D). SAGE convention for SubhaloVelDisp is the 1D dispersion (sigma_1D = sigma_3D / sqrt(3)). Since SubhaloVelDisp is optional and not used for baryonic physics, sigV is written directly without the sqrt(3) correction. See known_caveats.

SubhaloVMax.notes: Column 17 in AHF_halos. AHF Vmax = sqrt(V2_max * phi_fac) where V2_max is the peak of GM(<r)/r - this is the correct max circular velocity definition matching the SAGE convention.

SubhaloSpin.source_field: lambda, Lx, Ly, Lz, Mhalo, Rhalo
SubhaloSpin.source_units: lambda: dimensionless; Lx/Ly/Lz: unit vector; Mhalo: Msun/h; Rhalo: kpc/h
SubhaloSpin.conversion_expr: j_mag = lambda * sqrt(2 * G_phys * Mhalo * (Rhalo / 1000)) * 1000; SubhaloSpin = stack([j_mag*Lx, j_mag*Ly, j_mag*Lz], axis=1); where G_phys = 4.3009e-9 (Mpc/h)(km/s)^2(Msun/h)^-1
SubhaloSpin.notes: AHF stores AngMom as a UNIT VECTOR (direction cosines, cols 22-24 in AHF_halos) normalized by |L|; the magnitude information is encoded in lambda (col 20, Bullock-style spin parameter: lambda = |L_code| / (M_vir_code * sqrt(2 * M_vir_code * R_vir_code)) with G=1 in code units). The specific angular momentum magnitude is reconstructed from the physical definition: lambda = |j| / sqrt(2 * G * M_vir * R_vir), so |j| = lambda * sqrt(2 * G * Mhalo * Rhalo_Mpc_h). G = 4.3009e-9 (Mpc/h)(km/s)^2(Msun/h)^-1. Rhalo from col 12 is in kpc/h; divide by 1000 to get Mpc/h. Multiply final result by 1000 to convert from (Mpc/h)(km/s) to (kpc/h)(km/s). The direction is given by the unit vector (Lx, Ly, Lz). Output shape (N, 3). See known_caveats for the lambda reconstruction caveat. On-disk values in (kpc/h)(km/s): lhalo_hdf5 reader multiplies by 0.001; binary_writer divides by 1000 before packing.

SubhaloIDMostBound.notes: Not available in standard AHF_halos output. The most-bound particle index is tracked internally but not written to the per-snapshot catalogue. Using sentinel value -1 (int64).

SnapNum.source_units: integer snapshot index encoded in HaloID
SnapNum.conversion_expr: snap_id = int(HaloID // int(1e16)); SnapNum = snap_id - min_snap_id
SnapNum.notes: AHF SUSSING2013 halo IDs encode the snapshot number: snap_id = floor(HaloID / 1e16). For this dataset, snaps run from 5 (z=29.079) to 56 (z=0.000), giving 52 snapshots. SnapNum is made zero-based by subtracting the minimum snap index (5): SnapNum = snap_id - 5, range [0, 51]. The min_snap_id is determined at runtime from the filenames.

FileNr.notes: Not applicable for AHF multi-snapshot ASCII format; the converter merges all snapshots into a single output file. Using sentinel value -1.

pointer_logic.description: AHF/MergerTree does not produce pre-built LHaloTree pointer arrays. The driver must construct merger trees from scratch by (1) parsing all per-snapshot AHF_halos files and (2) parsing all AHF_croco progenitor-link files. Halo IDs follow the SUSSING2013 encoding: ID = snap_id * 1e16 + mpi_rank * 1e10 + halo_1based_index. Progenitor links in AHF_croco run backwards in time: each file for snapshot N lists, for every snap-N halo, all snap-(N-1) halos that share particles with it, sorted by merit descending. The driver inverts these to obtain descendant links, then identifies connected trees by DFS from snap-N_max roots, assigns flat tree-local indices, and builds all five SAGE pointer fields.
pointer_logic.step1_parse_catalogues: For each snapshot S from snap_min to snap_max, parse the corresponding AHF_halos file. Store per-halo: HaloID, Mhalo, npart, Xc/Yc/Zc, VXc/VYc/VZc, Vmax, sigV, lambda, Lx/Ly/Lz, Rhalo, hostHaloID, SnapNum. Build a global dict halo_props[HaloID] = {...}.
pointer_logic.step2_parse_croco: For each AHF_croco file (snap N, N from snap_min+1 to snap_max): parse every descendant block. Build progenitors[desc_ID] = [(merit1, prog_ID1), (merit2, prog_ID2), ...] sorted by merit descending. Simultaneously build descendants[prog_ID] = desc_ID (keep highest-merit descendant if a prog_ID appears under multiple desc_IDs, which should not occur with MTREE_BOTH_WAYS but is possible otherwise).
pointer_logic.step3_identify_trees: Starting from all halos at snap_max (z=0) that have no descendant entry in the descendants dict, perform a DFS/BFS backwards through progenitors to collect all temporally connected halos into a single tree. Halos at earlier snapshots with no descendant (orphan halos - e.g. from snap-skipping that was never resolved) are each placed in their own singleton tree. Process trees in order of decreasing Mhalo of the snap_max root.
pointer_logic.step4_assign_indices: Within each tree, assign flat integer indices [0, N_tree-1]. The ordering is: all halos sorted first by SnapNum descending (z=0 first, high-z last), then by Mhalo descending within each snapshot. This places the z=0 root at index 0 and ensures temporal consistency.
pointer_logic.Descendant: For each halo H in the tree, look up descendants[H.HaloID]. If found, map the result HaloID to its flat index via haloID_to_flat_index[desc_HaloID]. If not found (H is a root), set Descendant[H] = -1.
pointer_logic.FirstProgenitor: For each halo H: if H.HaloID is in progenitors and the list is non-empty, FirstProgenitor[H] = haloID_to_flat_index[progenitors[H.HaloID][0][1]] (the highest-merit progenitor). Otherwise -1.
pointer_logic.NextProgenitor: For each halo H with k>=2 progenitors [P0, P1, ..., Pk-1] sorted by merit descending: NextProgenitor[flat_index(P0)] = flat_index(P1), NextProgenitor[flat_index(P1)] = flat_index(P2), ..., NextProgenitor[flat_index(Pk-1)] = -1. Progenitors of H that have no sibling (k=1 or last in list) get NextProgenitor = -1.
pointer_logic.FirstHaloInFOFGroup: For each halo H at snapshot S: trace the hostHaloID chain upwards (hostHaloID != 0) until reaching the top-level central C (hostHaloID == 0). FirstHaloInFOFGroup[H] = haloID_to_flat_index[C.HaloID]. For a top-level central, FirstHaloInFOFGroup[C] = flat_index(C) (self-pointer). Cache the top-central result per halo to avoid repeated traversal (O(N) total with memoization).
pointer_logic.NextHaloInFOFGroup: For each snapshot S, group all halos by their top-level central HaloID. Within each group, sort by Mhalo descending (central first, then satellites by decreasing mass). Build the singly-linked chain: central.NextHaloInFOFGroup = flat_index(sat1), sat1.NextHaloInFOFGroup = flat_index(sat2), ..., last_sat.NextHaloInFOFGroup = -1. Halos with no group members other than themselves also get NextHaloInFOFGroup = -1.

simulation_params.particle_mass_note: Confirmed from B25_N512_CDM_3LPT_z39_adapt.gizmo_parameters: Omega0=0.3099, BoxSize=25 Mpc/h, N=512^3. Formula: 0.3099 * 2.775e11 * 25^3 / 512^3 = 1.001e7 Msun/h. Matches driver estimate from Mhalo/npart.

known_caveats: SubhaloSpin is reconstructed from AHF's lambda spin parameter and AngMom unit vector. AHF stores AngMom as a UNIT VECTOR (direction cosines), not as specific angular momentum. The magnitude is reconstructed using the physical formula |j| = lambda * sqrt(2G * Mhalo * Rhalo_Mpc_h) with G = 4.3009e-9 (Mpc/h)(km/s)^2(Msun/h)^-1. This reconstruction is physically correct given the AHF lambda definition (confirmed from source: ahf_halos.c line 4952) but introduces dependence on Mhalo and Rhalo. Any uncertainty in these fields propagates to SubhaloSpin.

SubhaloVelDisp is mapped from AHF's sigV, which is the 3D RMS velocity dispersion (sigma_3D = sqrt(sum(|dV|^2 * w) / M), confirmed from ahf_halos.c line 4687). SAGE convention is the 1D dispersion (sigma_1D = sigma_3D / sqrt(3)). Since SubhaloVelDisp is optional and not used for SAGE baryonic physics, sigV is written directly.

Group_M_Mean200 and Group_M_TopHat200 are not available in AHF output. AHF computes a single virial mass using one overdensity criterion (here: M_200c, ovdens=200 critical). Both fields use sentinel 0.0.
SubhaloIDMostBound is not written to standard AHF_halos output. Sentinel -1 is used.

AHF snap-skipping: when MergerTree cannot find a progenitor at the immediately preceding snapshot, it searches further back in time. Progenitor-descendant links may therefore span non-adjacent snapshots. Such halos will have SnapNum values that differ by more than 1 across a Descendant-FirstProgenitor link, which is unusual but valid for SAGE (SAGE uses SnapNum to order halos temporally, not to enforce strict adjacency).

AHF hostHaloID encodes a multi-level subhalo hierarchy (sub-sub-halos etc.). The driver flattens this to a two-level structure for SAGE (top-level central + all satellites at any depth). Sub-subhalo hierarchical structure is not preserved in SAGE's FOF group chain.

The SUSSING2013 halo ID encoding assumes the AHF run used WITH_MPI: ID = snap_id * 1e16 + mpi_rank * 1e10 + halo_1based_index. For a single-process run (no MPI), the encoding is snap_id * 1e12 + halo_1based_index (from specific.c line 2150). The data files for this dataset use the MPI encoding (snap IDs visible as the leading two digits of 18-digit IDs), which the driver auto-detects by checking whether floor(ID / 1e16) yields a plausible snapshot number.

The AHF_croco files list progenitors ordered by merit at the time of writing, which is SharedPart / min(HaloPart_desc, HaloPart_prog) or a variant - the exact merit formula depends on the MergerTree compile-time flags. The driver treats the order as merit-descending and assigns FirstProgenitor to the first-listed progenitor, consistent with the AHF convention.

Flyby handling is OPT-IN via sim_params['merge_flybys'] (default off), same as the Consistent-Trees driver. An AHF union-find tree can contain more than one independent z=0 central. Enabling merge_flybys folds the non-dominant z=0 centrals into the most massive one (reproducing SAGE's fix_flybys); default OFF keeps them as independent Type-0 centrals. This is a modelling choice that changes the z=0 population, not a bug fix.
